members whose e-mail address is registered with the Company / Company's Registrar and Transfer Agent /

scheduled to be held on Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 3:00 P.M. (IST) through Video Conferencing 
(VC)/Other Audio Visual Means (OAVM) facility to transact the Ordinary and Special business(es) as set out in 
the Notice of 42ndAGM in compliance with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and other relevant circulars issued by the MCA and 
the SEBI, from time to time.  
The Company is providing remote e-Voting and e-Voting facility at 42nd AGM to the members through electronic 
voting platform of KFIN Technologies Limited (“KFIN”). Members holding shares either in physical form or 
dematerialized form as on cut-off date i.e. Wednesday, September 16, 2026 may cast their votes electronically 
on the resolutions included in the Notice of 42nd AGM. The remote e-Voting shall commence from 09:00 A.M.  
(IST) on Saturday,  September 19, 2026 and shall end at 05:00 P.M.  (IST) on Tuesday, September 22, 2026 .                
The instructions on the process of e-voting, including the manner in which the members holding shares in 
physical form or who have not registered their e-mail address can cast their vote through e-voting, has been 
provided as part of Notice of 42nd AGM.

BORDERLESS SERVICES, 
BOUNDLESS GROWTH
We live in an era defined by movement. Citizens cross borders for work, for family, for education, for aspiration.  
Yet the systems governments built to serve them were designed for a different world — one where most people stayed. 
The gap between what citizens now expect and what legacy government infrastructure can deliver is no longer a passing 
inefficiency. It is a structural reality, growing wider with every passing year.
In response, governments across the world are drawing a new line — between sovereign decision-making, which must 
remain with the state, and service delivery, which can be done with greater reach, speed, and care by partners who have 
made it their entire purpose. This is not privatisation. It is precision — a recognition that governments serve citizens best 
when they trust the right things to the right hands.
Technology has deepened this shift. Artificial intelligence, biometrics, and digital platforms now make 
it possible to bring a government service to anyone, anywhere — without sacrificing the sovereignty, 
security, or trust that define the relationship between a state and its people. Governments are no longer 
outsourcing only for cost. They are outsourcing for capability — for partners who understand that every 
interaction is, ultimately, an act of governance.
This is that gave rise to this year’s theme. “Borderless Services, Boundless Growth” is not a celebration 
of scale already achieved. It is a standard — a declaration that services must follow the citizen, not wait 
for them; that quality must not vary by geography; and that growth, when rooted in genuine purpose, 
finds no natural ceiling.
The global infrastructure for citizen services is being rebuilt — technology by technology, partnership by 
partnership, country by country. To operate at this frontier is to help shape what it means, for the next 
generation, to be served by a government that can truly reach you — wherever you are.“The best services do not stop at a border. 
And the best partners do not either.”
Services that know no borders.
Growth that knows no ceiling.
A purpose that knows 
exactly where it is going.Theme Introduction

OUR STORY, 
OUR PURPOSEOUR CORE PRINCIPLESABOUT US
BLS International is one of the world’s top-2 comprehensive end-to-end solution provider, catering to the evolving needs 
of governments and citizens across global markets. As the only publicly listed company in this domain, BLS International manages visa outsourcing, consular services, and digital citizen services at scale — having processed over 490 million applications to date. The company combines two decades of expertise with a technology-driven, asset-light model that creates high entry barriers and durable government relationships.
BLS International operates two complementary segments — Visa & Consular Services, its high-margin core business, 
and Digital Services (via 52%-owned BLS E-Services), a fast-scaling platform serving rural India and financial inclusion. 
Backed by a workforce of over 63,000  employees and professionals, an extensive global delivery network, and more than 
1,55,000 citizen service touchpoints across India, BLS International continues to deliver trusted, technology-enabled services at scale. Its globally recognised certifications underscore a steadfast commitment to quality, security, and operational excellence.
Recognised among India’s most valuable companies and featured in leading global business rankings, BLS International 
has built its reputation on long-standing government partnerships and consistent execution. As the Company enters its third decade, it remains committed to advancing citizen service delivery through innovation, digital transformation, and enduring trust.Innovation drives our growth and service excellence. Through AI-enabled platforms, biometric technologies, multilingual support, and proprietary digital solutions, we are enhancing efficiency, security, and customer convenience across visa, consular, and citizen services.Trust is the foundation of our business. Backed by global standards such as GDPR and ISO 27001, we maintain robust data security, stringent compliance protocols, and secure digital infrastructure, reinforcing our position as a trusted government partner.
We are committed to fostering inclusive growth by expanding access to essential services. Through our Business Correspondent network, we promote financial inclusion, support local entrepreneurship, and create sustainable livelihood opportunities in underserved communities.Our people are at the centre of our success. By nurturing a diverse, inclusive, and learning-driven workplace, we empower employees to innovate, grow, and contribute meaningfully to our long-term success.

OUR STRATEGIC 
STRENGTHSOUR CORE COMPETENCIES
Our core competencies form the foundation of our competitive advantage, enabling us to consistently deliver 
value, drive innovation, and adapt to evolving market needs. Built on deep expertise, operational excellence, and a customer-centric approach, these strengths position us to capitalize on opportunities and sustain long-term growth.
Comprehensive Government-
to-Citizen Service Portfolio
BLS International delivers an 
end-to-end suite of government-to-citizen services spanning visa processing, consular support, document attestation, passport renewals, biometric enrolment, and citizenship and residency by investment programs. Trusted by over 46 governments and operating in 100+ countries, the Company serves as a strategic partner to diplomatic missions and government institutions, enabling them to focus entirely on decision-making while we manage the full administrative lifecycle.Regulatory Compliance as a Competitive Advantage
Operating in sovereign, 
data-sensitive environments demands the highest compliance standards. Our governance framework is backed by internationally recognised certifications — ISO 27001:2022, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO 31000:2018, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, CMMI DEV V2.0 Level 5, and ISAE 3402 Type II — making compliance not just a requirement, but a durable barrier to entry.Digital and AI-Led Excellence
Technology is at the heart 
of our service delivery. Our platforms incorporate AI-driven document authentication, advanced biometric and fingerprint verification, multi-level blockchain security, Optical Character Recognition-based processing, and Natural Language Processing for multilingual citizen engagement. These capabilities reduce turnaround times, enhance fraud prevention, and ensure a seamless applicant experience at scale.Customised Citizen Solutions
We develop tailor-made 
service solutions for missions, consulates, banks, and financial institutions, integrating seamlessly with government frameworks while addressing the nuanced needs of citizens across geographies. Our IT infrastructure enables rapid customisation of platforms to meet diverse client requirements without compromising on security or scale.Operational Excellence Through an Asset-Light Model
Our self-managed, asset-light 
operating model is designed for agility and scalability. In FY26, the Visa & Consular segment achieved an EBITDA margin of 40.1%, reflecting years of disciplined transition from partner-run centres to fully self-managed hubs, strategic cost optimisation, and technology-enabled workflow automation. Strong Future Pipeline and Balance Sheet
With net cash of Rs. 1,434 
crores as of March 2026, zero receivables from missions and embassies, and a negative working capital model, BLS International enters its next phase of growth from a position of financial strength. Major contracts worth USD 1–2 billion are due for renewal in the near term, alongside significant new opportunities in the UIDAI/Aadhaar infrastructure and global visa outsourcing markets

WHAT WE DELIVERABOUT OUR OFFERINGS
As one of the world’s leading providers of AI & technology-enabled citizen 
and government services, BLS International delivers comprehensive solutions that simplify global mobility and public service access. Our integrated offerings span across visa, consular, digital, and citizen services, enabling seamless, secure, and efficient experiences for governments and citizens across the world.
Operating across 100+ countries in partnership with 46+ client governments, BLS International manages all 
administrative and non-judgmental tasks for governments and diplomatic missions, allowing them to focus entirely on visa application assessment and sovereign decision-making. Our three core offering pillars — Visa & Allied Services, Consular Services, and E-Visa Services — work in seamless concert to deliver a world-class, one-stop service experience.
The cornerstone of Company’s global service portfolio
Visa & Allied Services form the bedrock of BLS International’s business, representing Rs. 1,840 Crores in revenue for FY26 — growing at a CAGR of 25% since FY22. BLS International manages the entire front-end of the visa application process on behalf of its client governments, handling every administrative and logistical element that allows embassies and consulates to focus exclusively on visa adjudication.
BLS International holds 17% Market Share by Value and 10% by Volume in the Global Visa Outsourcing Market 
(excluding USA) in 2024 — a testament to the scale, trust and operational excellence built over two decades of global service delivery.

THE INVESTMENT 
OPPORTUNITYINVESTMENT CASE
BLS International offers a compelling investment proposition, underpinned by a scalable business model, 
strong global presence, diversified service portfolio, and proven execution capabilities. Positioned at the intersection of growing global mobility and digital citizen services, the Company is well placed to capitalize on emerging opportunities, drive sustainable growth, and create long-term value for its stakeholders.FOCUS ON PROFITABLE GROWTH
BLS International has consistently converted revenue scale into margin expansion — a rare combination in services 
businesses. The shift from a partner-run model to self-managed operations, combined with deepening technology leverage, has structurally re-rated the cost base. Margins are not a temporary outcome; they reflect a deliberate operating architecture built over years.
EXCLUSIVE & LONG-TERM CONTRACTS
Government outsourcing contracts are not transactional — they are structural embeds. Once a visa application 
infrastructure is live in a country, displacement is operationally, diplomatically, and contractually difficult. BLS International benefits from exclusive mandates with no vendor overlap, and contracts that run 5 to 10 years —  creating multi-year revenue visibility that is structurally rare in services
WHAT EXCLUSIVITY MEANS IN PRACTICE
•
 No competing vendor in the same region — pricing 
 and volume are ring-fenced
• Long contract tenures underpin revenue predictability  
 and margin planning
• Renewal cycles create a known pipeline: major   
 contracts worth USD 1–2 billion due in the next 
 two years
• Deep integration with government workflows creates 
 high switching costs for clients
STRONG FUTURE VISIBILITY
The tailwinds for BLS International are not cyclical 
— they are structural and compounding. Global cross-border mobility is rising. Governments are progressively outsourcing more citizen service categories. AI and digital infrastructure are expanding the scope of what outsourcing partners can offer. BLS International sits at the intersection of all three.FORWARD VISIBILITY DRIVERS
•
 USD 1–2 bil lion in contract renewals due within two  
 years — not new business, but known pipeline

• Inorganic pipeline: M&A opportunities in Visa &   
 Consular segment being as sessedASSET-LIGHT MODELBLS International does not own the real estate it operates 
from — every Visa Application Centre globally is on lease. Capital is deployed primarily into technology, talent, and capability rather than fixed assets. The Digital Services business runs on a merchant-led model — growth is delivered through a network of business correspondents and citizen service touchpoints, not through owned infrastructure. This means scale amplifies returns, rather than consuming them.
The business model also carries a structural cash 
advantage: processing fees are collected upfront — before services are rendered. This creates negative working capital and zero receivables from embassies and missions, making BLS International a naturally cash-generative business at every stage of growth.

Annual Report 2025-26BUILDING RESILIENCE, 
DELIVERING GROWTHMD’s Message
Nikhil Gupta 
Managing Director
BLS International Services Ltd.NAVIGATING A VOLATILE WORLD
FY 2025-26 unfolded against one of the most testing 
geopolitical backdrops in recent memory. Prolonged tensions across the Middle East, shifting trade policies, and the ripple effects of global macro volatility created an operating environment that tested the resilience of businesses across industries. For a company like BLS International Services Ltd. that operates across 100+ countries and is deeply intertwined with the movement of people and governments, these were not distant risks-they were real, present challenges.
Yet, FY 2025-26 stands as perhaps our most emphatic 
demonstration of what it means to be a purpose-built, structurally resilient business. While geopolitical disruptions caused temporary shifts in travel patterns - particularly in the Middle East corridor - the company did not witness a meaningful revenue impact. Our diversified geographic presence across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas acted as a natural hedge, ensuring that no single region’s turbulence could derail the broader performance of the enterprise. The strength of our exclusive, long-term government contracts further insulated our revenue streams from short-term disruptions.
This is not resilience by accident. It is resilience by design—
built deliberately through years of disciplined execution, diversified expansion, and a business model that is structurally decoupled from cyclical volatility.  FY 2025-26 is the proof.The strategic foundation we laid over the preceding years—transitioning to a self-managed centre model, embedding technology at every service touchpoint, and building a diversified government partnership portfolio—continued to pay dividends in FY 2025-26. The full-year consolidation of Aadifidelis Solutions accelerated the scale of our Digital Services segment, which crossed the Rs. 1,000 Crores milestone for the first time. Simultaneously, our Visa & Consular Services business delivered its best-ever EBITDA margin of 40.1%, reflecting the compounding benefits of operational control and pricing maturity.
The company also made significant strides on the contract 
front. The UIDAI work order of Rs. 2,055 Crores for Aadhaar Seva Kendras represents a landmark entry into the onshore citizen service delivery space. Combined with new visa outsourcing mandates from Slovakia, Cyprus, and the Ministry of External Affairs for Indian Visa Application Centres in China, the company has meaningfully expanded both its revenue visibility and its footprint in high-potential geographies. These wins are not opportunistic—they are the outcome of years of institutional credibility, operational excellence, and investment in technology and compliance infrastructure.
CAPITAL DISCIPLINE AND BALANCE SHEET 
STRENGTH
FY 2025-26 marked a year of exceptional cash generation. 
Operating cash flows of Rs. 903 Crores resulted in a net cash balance of Rs. 1,434 Crores as on 31st March 2026—an increase of over Rs. 500 Crores year-on-year. This demonstrates the inherent cash-generative capacity of the company’s asset-light, negative working capital business model.
Capital allocation remained disciplined and purposeful. 
The UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra project (Rs. 2,055 Crores work order) and the Bihar Government’s Permanent Enrolment Centres for Aadhaar project (Rs. 100 Crores) represent high-conviction, execution-ready investments in the onshore citizen services space. These are being funded through internal accruals, consistent with the company’s philosophy of growth without compromising balance sheet integrity.
In recognition of the company’s strong financial 
performance and its commitment to rewarding shareholders, the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.50 per equity share (50% of face value). Combined with the interim dividend of Rs. 2.00 per equity share already paid during the year, the total dividend payout stands at Rs. 2.50 per share—representing 250% of face value—with a total outflow of over Rs. 100 Crores for the year.OVERVIEW
At BLS International, we have long believed that sustainable growth is forged not in favourable conditions alone, but in the discipline with which one navigates adversity. Over FY 2025-26, our team remained focused, agile, and committed. We deepened our operational capabilities, sharpened our financial discipline, and continued to invest in the infrastructure that will underpin the next decade of growth. The outcome is a year of consistent, broad-based performance that we present with quiet confidence.

GOVERNANCE, SUSTAINABILITY & 
RESPONSIBILITY
Sound governance is not a periodic requirement at BLS 
International—it is embedded in how The Company operates day to day. During FY 2025-26, the company continued to strengthen its internal control frameworks, compliance mechanisms, and risk management architecture to keep pace with the increasing scale and geographic complexity of its business.
Data privacy and information security continued to 
receive priority attention, with the company operating in accordance with internationally recognised standards across its multi-jurisdictional footprint. The company’s operating model is fully compliant with GDPR requirements, and its certifications across ISO 27001, ISO 9001, ISO 14001, CMMI, and ENS frameworks were maintained and revalidated during the year.
The company’s ESG commitment continued to deepen in 
FY 2025-26. CSR initiatives remained focused on women empowerment, financial literacy, and digital access for underserved communities, with total Group CSR contributions reflecting continued growth year-on-year. The company also maintained meaningful progress on its environmental management commitments, with ongoing efforts to reduce energy intensity and manage Scope 2 emissions across its global operations.
PEOPLE FIRST
At BLS International, our people are the engine of our growth. The company’s workforce—spanning 63,000+ professionals across 100+ countries—continued to be the differentiating factor in our ability to serve governments and citizens with consistency, precision, and empathy.
Structured leadership development programmes, including 
LEAP for first-time managers and LEAD for experienced leaders, continued to build depth in the leadership pipeline. The company’s Learning Management System and Project ELUVATE platform provided 21,000+ learning modules to employees across functions and geographies. Talent retention, career progression frameworks, and a culture of recognition remained central to the company’s People agenda in FY 2025-26.
OUTLOOK
As we enter FY 2026-27, BLS International is positioned at an inflection point of scale and strategic opportunity. The momentum across both business verticals is strong, our balance sheet is the most robust in the company’s history, and our pipeline of new contracts and renewals provides meaningful revenue visibility over the medium term.KEY PRIORITIES FOR THE YEAR AHEAD

GROWING WITH PURPOSE. 
DELIVERING WITH EXCELLENCE. BUILDING FOR THE FUTURE.JOINT MD’S PERSPECTIVE
When I reflect on BLS International’s performance in FY 
2025-26, I see far more than a year of strong financial results. I see an organisation that remained focused amidst uncertainty, executed with discipline, and continued to raise the bar for operational excellence and innovation.
The year marked another significant milestone in our 
growth journey. We delivered record financial performance, secured strategically important mandates, expanded our global footprint, and further strengthened our leadership position across both Visa & Consular Services and Digital Services. These achievements reflect the trust placed in us by governments and institutions worldwide, as well as the unwavering commitment of our teams who deliver excellence every day, across geographies and cultures.
What makes this performance particularly noteworthy is 
the backdrop against which it was achieved. Geopolitical tensions, evolving travel patterns, economic uncertainty, and regional disruptions continued to shape the global operating environment. Yet, BLS International’s diversified presence across more than 100+ countries, long-standing government partnerships, and resilient business model enabled us to navigate these challenges effectively. Having successfully weathered global crises, pandemics, financial downturns, and geopolitical disruptions over the years, we have built an organisation that remains agile, adaptable, and resilient. FY 2025-26 was another demonstration of that strength. We continued to grow, secure new mandates, and create value for all stakeholders.
GROWTH BELONGS TO THOSE WHO SEE OPPORTUNITY IN 
EVERY CHALLENGE.

POWERING PROFITABLE, 
PREDICTABLE AND DURABLE GROWTHCFO’S INSIGHTS
36 Annual Report 2025-26Dear Stakeholders,
FY 2025–26 was a year in which BLS International demonstrated, with rigour and consistency, that our financial architecture 
is built for the long run. We grew revenues by 36.7% to Rs. 2,998 Crores, expanded absolute EBITDA by 30.1% to Rs. 819 Crores, and delivered a Profit After Tax of Rs. 724 Crores — a 34.1% year-on-year increase. What makes these numbers particularly meaningful is what lies beneath them: an operating model that generates cash organically, requires minimal incremental capital, and compounds value across cycles.
We operate with a simple philosophy: growth must pay for itself. Every rupee we invest is backed by organic cash generation, 
every expansion is funded by our own strength, and every milestone is achieved without diluting shareholder value.
As CFO, my responsibility is not only to report growth, but to explain its quality, durability, and structural underpinnings. This 
year, I am proud to say that each of those three dimensions strengthened.
CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
The headline numbers tell a compelling story, but the details tell a better one. Revenue of Rs. 2,998 Crores was driven by a combination of organic volume growth in our Visa & Consular business — where applications processed grew 17.6% to 44.1 lakhs — and the first full-year consolidation of Aadifidelis Solutions within Digital Services. Crucially, this revenue is high-quality: it is diversified across 46 client governments, underpinned by exclusive long-term contracts of 5–10 years, and collected upfront before a single service is rendered. This upfront collection model is the structural reason our working capital is persistently negative — a rare financial trait that is a direct driver of our industry-leading cash conversion.
Amit Sudhakar
Chief Financial OfficerBLS International Services 
Limited
EBITDA of Rs. 819 Crores at a 27.3% margin warrants 
careful contextualisation. Last year, our EBITDA margin was 28.7% — and the natural question is whether this 140 basis point moderation signals a structural shift. It does not. The margin movement reflects the deliberate consolidation of Aadifidelis, a high-growth Digital Services business currently operating at a 7% EBITDA margin as it scales. Excluding this effect, our core Visa & Consular margin expanded from 34.5% to an exceptional 40.1% — a 560 basis point improvement in a single year.The Visa & Consular margin trajectory is the clearest evidence of our operating model maturity. From 14.6% in FY22 to 40.1% in FY26, this is not margin expansion driven by pricing alone. It reflects the compounding benefits of transitioning from partner-run to self-managed operations, disciplined fixed-cost management, and technology-driven throughput gains — specifically, our net revenue per application grew 13.7% to Rs. 3,302 this year, meaning we are extracting more value from every interaction without a proportional rise in cost.

38 Annual Report 2025-26VISA & CONSULAR: PRICING POWER MEETS 
VOLUME GROWTH
The Visa & Consular business is firing on all cylinders. 
Revenue grew 11.3% to Rs. 1,840 Crores, but the more instructive metric is net revenue — revenue after pass-through costs — which grew 33.8% to Rs. 1,457 Crores. This divergence between gross and net revenue growth tells us something important: we are not just processing more applications, we are structurally improving the economics of each application through better contract terms, higher Value Added Service attachment, and reduced partner dependency. The net revenue per application of Rs. 3,302 versus Rs. 2,903 last year is the clearest numerical expression of this.
DIGITAL SERVICES: SCALE FIRST, MARGIN TO 
FOLLOW
Digital Services revenue of Rs. 1,158 Crores represents 
114.4% growth, with EBITDA of Rs. 81 Crores growing 35.7%. The 7.0% EBITDA margin is intentional — this segment is in an investment phase, building touchpoints, integrating Aadifidelis, and establishing distribution depth across 1,55,000+ customer touchpoints. The operating model here is merchant-led and asset-light, meaning that as volumes compound, incremental margins will disproportionately flow to the bottom line. We are building the base; the harvest follows.
CASH GENERATION AND BALANCE SHEET 
STRENGTH
If there is one metric I would ask every stakeholder to 
focus on, it is operating cash flow. In FY26, we generated Rs. 903 Crores from operating activities — up from Rs. 829 Crores last year. This is cash that required no external financing, no equity dilution, and no compromise on our investment agenda. It is the organic lifeblood of our business, and it grew because our Visa & Consular business continues to collect fees before it delivers services — a negative working capital model that is structurally rare and financially powerful.
Our net cash position strengthened from Rs. 928 Crores to 
Rs. 1,434 Crores — an increase of Rs. 506 Crores in a single year, even as we deployed Rs. 446 Crores in investing activities including property additions and term deposits. Total assets grew from Rs. 2,837 Crores to Rs. 3,770 Crores, while shareholders’ funds expanded from Rs. 1,690 Crores to Rs. 2,422 Crores. Our balance sheet is not just healthy — it is increasingly a competitive weapon, enabling us to pursue large government mandates, fund strategic acquisitions, and absorb macro shocks without accessing external capital.
Borrowings decreased from EUR 24.97 million to EUR 
21.33 million in actuals. However, due to the increase in the EUR/INR exchange rate, the translated value increased from ₹229 crore to ₹231 crore in Group consolidation., while finance costs fell from Rs. 27.8 Crores to Rs. 23.2 Crores — reflecting our deliberate deleveraging even as we scaled. The tax rate normalised at 9.2% of PBT, reflecting the benefit of our diversified international structure and efficient tax planning.CAPITAL ALLOCATION: DISCIPLINED, DELIBERATE, 
VALUE-ACCRETIVE
Capital allocation is the ultimate test of financial discipline, 
and FY26 demonstrates our philosophy clearly. We invested Rs. 137 Crores in property, plant, and equipment — a disciplined figure for a business of our scale, consistent with our asset-light philosophy where visa application centres are leased, not owned. Our major investing outflow of Rs. 31 Crores related to subsidiary acquisition payments from the prior year’s M&A activity, now largely integrated.
On capital returns, we paid Rs. 130 Crores in dividends in 
FY26 — a meaningful step-up from Rs. 21 Crores in FY25 — reflecting our confidence in the sustainability of our cash flows and our commitment to sharing value with shareholders. Return on Equity stood at 29.4%, maintaining our industry-leading position even as net worth itself expanded significantly to Rs. 2,463 Crores.
Looking ahead, with Rs. 1,434 Crores of net cash and Rs. 
903 Crores of annual operating cash generation, we have the capacity to simultaneously pursue the Rs. 2,055 Crores UIDAI mandate, invest in Digital Services scale-up, and actively scout further M&A opportunities — all without any dilutive capital raise. This is the financial foundation of our growth confidence.
CREDIT PROFILE AND FINANCIAL GOVERNANCE
Our CRISIL long-term credit rating of A+/Stable, first upgraded in FY25 and maintained through FY26, is not just a rating — it is external validation of everything we have built: consistent cash generation, conservative leverage, transparent governance, and a track record of delivering on our financial commitments. It also has practical value: it lowers our cost of capital, strengthens our positioning in large government tender processes, and signals to counterparties that BLS is a partner built for the long term.
Internally, our governance framework remains rigorous. Zero 
cases of financial fraud, zero bribery incidents, independent board-level oversight, and ISO 27001 certification for information security are not compliance checkboxes — they are the operating conditions that allow 46 sovereign governments to trust us with the personal data and biometrics of their citizens.
FINANCIAL OUTLOOK: THE STRUCTURAL CASE FOR 
CONTINUED COMPOUNDING
The financial case for BLS International’s next chapter rests 
on three structural pillars. First, the global visa outsourcing market is growing at a 14% CAGR through 2029, and BLS — with 17% market share by value — is positioned to capture a disproportionate share of that growth through new contract wins, renewals, and geographic expansion. Second, our contract renewal pipeline of USD 1–2 billion over the next two years represents near-term revenue visibility that is exceptionally rare for a business of our size. Third, the UIDAI order of Rs. 2,055 Crores for Aadhaar Seva Kendras creates a multi-year domestic revenue stream that diversifies and deepens our India exposure.
On margins, I expect the consolidated EBITDA margin to 
stabilise and gradually trend upward as Digital Services matures and our Visa & Consular business continues to benefit from operating leverage. The fixed-cost base grows slowly while revenues compound — this is the structural source of margin expansion, and it remains intact.
On capital, we will remain disciplined. Growth will be self-
funded through operating cash flows wherever possible. Acquisitions will be pursued only where they meet our strategic criteria: synergy with existing capabilities, a clear path to value creation, and pricing that respects our cost of capital. We will not grow for the sake of scale.
37% Revenue CAGR. 66% EBITDA CAGR. 60% PAT CAGR. 
All delivered over four years on a self-funded, asset-light model. The compounding is structural — and we believe the best chapters are still ahead.
IN CLOSING
Finance, at its best, is not about reporting the past — it is about building confidence in the future. The numbers in this report reflect a business that has earned the right to be ambitious: a business with a strong balance sheet, a cash-generative model, exclusive long-term contracts, and a management team that has demonstrated, year after year, that it can execute with both speed and discipline.
I am deeply grateful to our shareholders for their trust, 
to the Board for their counsel, to our banking partners for their support, and to every member of the BLS team whose daily execution turns strategy into these numbers. The confidence I have in FY 2026–27 and beyond is not optimism — it is a conclusion drawn from evidence.

LANDSCAPEMARKET OPPORTUNITY
BLS International operates at the intersection of global mobility, citizen services and digital governance—
three sectors supported by strong structural growth drivers. Rising international travel, increasing government outsourcing, accelerating digital transformation, and growing demand for investment migration solutions are creating significant opportunities across the Company’s core markets. With its global presence, established government partnerships and technology-led capabilities, BLS International is well-positioned to capitalise on these emerging opportunities and drive sustainable long-term growth.
Governments worldwide are facing increasing demand for citizen services amid resource constraints, evolving data 
privacy regulations and growing expectations for digital-first experiences. This is accelerating the outsourcing of non-sovereign, high-volume services such as visa processing, passport services, consular support, biometric enrolment and digital identity management. The global citizen services market is witnessing strong growth, driven by rapid digitalisation and AI adoption, while the outsourced consular services segment is expected to expand at over 30% CAGR through 2029. 
BLS International has expanded its addressable scope from visa processing to a broader G2C service platform. In FY26, 
the Company secured a ₹2,055 crore UIDAI work order for Aadhaar Seva Kendras, a ₹100 crore Bihar Government Permanent Enrolment Centre project, and renewal of Attestation & Apostille Services with India’s Ministry of External Affairs. The Company’s 11-step integrated service model — from enquiry to document return — offers governments a fully managed, single-vendor solution. Visa & Consular services EBITDA reached ₹738 crores in FY26, up 29.5% YoY. EXPANSION OF GOVERNMENT OUTSOURCING IN CITIZEN SERVICES

Global travel recovery continues to create significant growth opportunities, albeit at varying speeds across regions. The 
Middle East and Africa have surpassed pre-pandemic travel levels, supported by strong tourism and economic growth, while Asia-Pacific remains below 2019 benchmarks, offering substantial catch-up potential. Strengthening travel corridors, particularly between Europe and Asia, alongside robust economic growth in emerging markets and India’s position as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, are expected to support sustained growth in international mobility and visa demand.
In FY26, BLS International actively expanded across under-penetrated corridors: a 3-year contract from India’s MEA 
to operate Indian Visa Application Centres across China; a 5-year global contract from the Slovak Republic covering 100+ countries; Cyprus contracts spanning Russia, China, South Africa, Kazakhstan, and key Southeast Asian nations; and Hungary’s visa service expansion to Jordan, Canada, Algeria, and Oman. BLS International has existing operational presence across Africa — directly aligned with the region’s record aviation growth. The Company’s 100+ country footprint spans every high-growth corridor identified by IATA and UN Tourism.
Governments are increasingly prioritising service quality, data security and operational control when selecting outsourcing 
partners. This is driving a shift towards self-managed service delivery models that offer greater accountability, consistency and compliance. As outsourced service providers become deeply integrated into government workflows, high switching costs and long-term relationships create durable competitive advantages, raising barriers to entry and favouring established operators with strong infrastructure and execution capabilities.
BLS International’s transition from a partner-run to a fully self-managed VAC network is now substantially complete. Visa 
& Consular EBITDA margins expanded from 14.6% in FY22 to 40.1% in FY26 — a 2,553 basis point expansion — driven by reduced partner dependency, operating leverage, tighter operational control, and the elimination of intermediary costs. The self-managed model strengthens government trust and direct accountability — now explicit requirements in global tender evaluations.The global investment migration industry exceeded USD 30 billion in market value in 2024, growing at approximately 12% annually, with over 80 countries offering investment migration programmes. Wealth migration continues to accelerate, with 142,000 millionaires relocating globally in 2025 and 165,000 projected in 2026, driven by the pursuit of political stability, favourable tax regimes, quality healthcare, education and enhanced global mobility. Evolving regulatory frameworks are further increasing demand for specialised advisory services, creating significant opportunities for experienced investment migration providers.
The acquisition of Citizenship Invest marks our strategic entry into the investment migration sector, strengthening our 
portfolio with premium residency and citizenship solutions. This expansion enhances our ability to serve high-net-worth individuals while diversifying revenue streams through a high-value, globally scalable business.GEOGRAPHIC EXPANSION INTO EMERGING & UNDER PENETRATED MARKETS

NEGATIVE WORKING CAPITAL
BLS International operates a structurally cash-generative business model. This approach creates a negative working capital position — significantly strengthening liquidity and enabling efficient cash flow management across all geographies and operating conditions.

MANAGING RISK, 
SUSTAINING GROWTHRISK MANAGEMENT & MITIGATION
Risk management is a strategic cornerstone of BLS International’s operations and a key enabler of its long-term 
objectives. As a globally operating government services partner,  multiple regulatory jurisdictions, diverse geopolitical environments, and an increasingly digitalised service landscape — making a proactive, structured approach to risk identification, assessment and mitigation a business-critical capability.
Our risk management philosophy is anchored in three guiding principles: competitive and sustainable growth, responsible 
governance, and agility in an ever-evolving digital and geopolitical environment. Guided by these principles, our risk appetite is clearly defined, and strategic decisions across all business verticals — visa processing, digital services, consular operations and e-governance — are driven by a need for responsiveness, ethics and transparency.
Identify & Assess
Systematic identification and quantification of all material risks across geographies, business verticals and operational processes.Mitigate & Control
Implement robust controls, contingency plans and mitigation measures to reduce likelihood and impact of identified risks.Monitor & Improve
Continuous monitoring of the risk landscape, with quarterly Board reviews and regular updates to the risk register.Description Mitigation Risk
Regulatory Risk
Cybersecurity &

Global Geopolitical RiskChanges in visa regulations, 
immigration policies, outsourcing frameworks, or government procedures may affect business volumes and operations.
Cyber-attacks, data breaches, 
or system disruptions could impact operations, reputation and regulatory compliance.
Political instability, diplomatic 
tensions, travel restrictions or economic disruptions across operating geographies may impact demand and service delivery.BLS International has been systematically 
diversifying its service portfolio beyond traditional visa processing into e-governance, UIDAI services and digital financial inclusion, reducing dependence on any single contract or jurisdiction. The Company invests heavily in compliance readiness, maintaining ISO 9001, ISO 27001, CMMI Level 5 and ENS certifications. A dedicated tender management team actively tracks regulatory landscapes in all key geographies, with an aggressive bidding strategy underpinned by technology differentiation and established government relationships.
BLS International enforces stringent, 
multi-layered cybersecurity protocols across all operations. Key controls include: ISO 27001:2013-certified information security management, multi-factor authentication and end-to-end data encryption, regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing, blockchain-secured identity data handling, AI-powered anomaly detection, frequent IT audits aligned with CMMI Level 5 standards, and a comprehensive disaster recovery and business continuity framework. The Company has implemented a global data protection policy covering the full data lifecycle — classification, storage, transfer and disposal — achieving zero data breach incidents in FY26.
BLS International has built a well-
diversified global business portfolio serving 46+ client governments across 100+ countries, ensuring that regional disruptions have a limited impact on consolidated operations. The Digital Services segment, with Rs. 1,158 Crores revenue in FY26, provides meaningful counter-cyclical revenue resilience. The UIDAI contract (Rs. 2,055 Crores) further anchors domestic revenue stability. BLS’s asset-light model — with all VACs on operating leases — ensures rapid operational scalability and cost flexibility during demand downturns.

Currency Fluctuation RiskNon-renewal or delay in renewal

With operations spanning multiple 
geographies, BLS International is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations that may impact revenues, costs and reported financial performance. Variations in currency exchange rates could affect earnings from international operations and cross-border transactions.Diversified client portfolio across 46+ governments, proactive contract management, superior service standards, and continuous engagement with client governments to enhance retention and contract renewals.BLS International has established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), risk assessment frameworks, and contingency plans for all critical functions, ensuring business continuity across all geographies. The Smart Queue Management System (SQMS) and centralised document management systems provide real-time operational monitoring. The self-managed VAC model provides greater operational control compared to the previous partner-run structure, enabling faster identification and resolution of process gaps.
BLS International employs a 
currency hedging policy aligned with industry best practices to mitigate the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on receivables, projected revenue, and other current assets and liabilities. The hedging strategy is periodically reviewed and adjusted to align with prevailing market conditions. The Company’s negative working capital model — where processing fees are collected upfront before services are rendered — significantly reduces receivables exposure and limits the duration of currency risk on revenue streams.

GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
BLS keeps its Board deliberately tilted towards independence: Independent Directors hold more than half of all Board 
seats, the Chairperson role is Non-Executive, and the Board includes a woman Independent Director. That balance is meant to ensure decisions are shaped by outside judgement rather than by management alone.
Beyond independence, Directors are chosen for a spread of skills, sector backgrounds, and international exposure 
relevant to a company operating across 80-plus countries. GLOBAL ECONOMIC 
OVERVIEW
The global economy entered FY 2025–26 in cautious transition — more 
resilient than the headline risks suggested, yet more fragile than the headline numbers implied. A year shaped by escalating geopolitical tensions, sweeping tariff escalations and renewed supply-side shocks tested the durability of the post-pandemic recovery cycle.
The global economy navigated a complex and shifting landscape — one defined by the gradual unwinding of post-
pandemic imbalances, recalibration of global trade flows amid sweeping tariff escalations and rising geopolitical flashpoints across multiple regions. Despite these pressures, the world economy demonstrated underlying resilience, underpinned by robust activity in emerging markets, stabilising inflation trajectories and continued fiscal and monetary policy support across major jurisdictions.

OVERVIEW
India surpassed Japan to become the world's fourth-largest economy in 
nominal GDP terms in FY 2025–26 — and is projected to become the third largest by 2028, overtaking Germany.
India's real GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025–26 — accelerating from 7.1% in FY 2024–25 — while nominal GDP expanded 
8.6%, reaching ₹345.47 lakh crore. Growth was underpinned by healthy private consumption, sustained infrastructure investment, and strong momentum across services and industry.
India is projected to remain the fastest-growing major economy in FY 2026–27, with the IMF raising its real GDP forecast to 6.5% and the RBI projecting 6.9%. Real GDP growth was broad-based through FY 2025–26 — reflecting consistent sectoral momentum. An interim India–US trade deal in February 2026 reduced effective tariff duties from 50% to 18%, reducing a key near-term headwind. India is projected to become the world's third-largest economy by 2028, with the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision targeting a GDP of USD 30–40 trillion — reinforcing structural demand for cross-border mobility and digital citizen services, both core to BLS International's business.India's macroeconomic fundamentals remained resilient during FY2025–26. Foreign exchange reserves touched an all-time high of USD 728.49 billion earlier in FY2025–26, before moderating to USD 691.1 billion as at end-March 2026, reflecting sustained capital inflows and prudent reserve management by the Reserve Bank of India. Gross FDI inflows reached USD 88.29 billion during April 2025–February 2026, surpassing the full-year FY2024–25 inflows of USD 80.6 billion and reaffirming continued investor confidence. The current account deficit remained contained at around 1.0% of GDP, while the banking sector remained resilient, with the gross NPA ratio improving to 2.0% as of March 2026, supported by healthy credit growth and strengthening asset quality.GDP and Sectoral Performance

GLOBAL TRAVEL AND 
TOURISM INDUSTRY
The global travel and tourism industry delivered a landmark performance in CY2025, transitioning decisively from post-
pandemic restoration into structural expansion. Encompassing lodging, transportation, attractions, dining, and ancillary services, the sector's growth is being driven by rising cross-border mobility, accelerating digitalisation, and deepening global connectivity — creating a highly favourable operating environment for specialised players in visa outsourcing and consular services.
Its total contribution to global GDP reached a record USD 11.6 trillion — 9.8% of the world economy — growing at 4.1%, 
nearly 50% faster than overall global economic growth of 2.8%, making Travel and Tourism the world's fastest-growing major sector.International tourist arrivals reached 1.465 billion in 2024 — essentially recovering to the 2019 peak — before breaking through to a new record of 1.523 billion in 2025, up 4% year-on-year. CY2025 marks the first full post-pandemic year, conclusively above the 2019 high. Demand is now self-sustaining — driven by normalised mobility, emerging market outbound growth, and the structural rise in experiential travel, rather than post-pandemic pent-up demand.
The global Travel and Tourism industry generated total visitor spending of USD 7.65 trillion in CY2025 — comprising USD 5.63 trillion in domestic spending and USD 2.02 trillion in international visitor spending. International tourism receipts reached USD 1.9 trillion, growing faster than arrival volumes (+5% vs +4%), confirming the industry is extracting higher yield per traveller even as volume growth normalises. Total tourism export revenues including passenger transport reached USD 2.2 trillion.OVERVIEWTHE GLOBAL TOURISM RECOVERY ARC — 2019 TO 2025

Recovery patterns remained structurally uneven across regions through 2024 and 2025. The Middle East led in absolute 
recovery terms — reaching 39% above 2019 levels by 2025 — while Africa posted the fastest regional growth rate in 2025 at 10%, reaching 17% above its 2019 baseline. Asia-Pacific, despite leading aviation RPK growth, recorded 8% arrival growth but remained approximately 10% below 2019 — representing the sector's largest and most commercially significant catch-up opportunity.Global full-year air passenger demand in 2025, measured in Revenue Passenger Kilometres (RPK), rose 5.3% year-on-year, while Available Seat Kilometres (ASK) expanded 5.2% to — both at historic highs. The Passenger Load Factor (PLF) reached a record of 83.6%, reflecting structural tightening of the supply-demand balance as aerospace supply chain disruptions delayed new aircraft deliveries.
Asia-Pacific accounts for 34.5% of global RPK — the largest regional share — and delivered total RPK growth of 7.8% 
in 2025, with international RPK expanding at an even faster 10.9%, both comfortably above the global averages of 5.3% and 7.1% respectively. The region's international PLF reached 84.4% in 2025, the highest among all regions. This momentum carried into 2026, with Asia-Pacific carriers recording 11.5% RPK growth in March 2026 and a record international PLF of 91.2% — the highest of any region globally. The Europe–Asia corridor surged 29.3% in March 2026, partly reflecting traffic diverted from disrupted Middle Eastern hubs. For BLS, Asia-Pacific remains the sector's largest catch-up opportunity and this sustained outperformance reinforces both the scale of addressable demand and the strategic priority of the region.
Africa led all regions in total RPK growth in 2025 at 9.4% — the highest annual growth rate globally — with international 
RPK expanding 7.8% and PLF improving 0.7 percentage points to 75.3%. This outperformance accelerated sharply into 2026, with African carriers posting 20.6% RPK growth in March 2026 — more than nine times the global average of 2.1% — a trend sustained consistently since August 2024. International capacity from Africa grew at just 4.2% against demand growth of 19.2% in March 2026, pushing PLF up nearly 10 percentage points to 77.7% — a record high for the region, signalling structural demand expansion well ahead of supply. BLS's established operational presence across Africa positions the Company directly within this growth corridor, with service demand expanding in step with rising cross-border passenger flows.Asia-Pacific — Largest Catch-Up Opportunity: 316 Mn arrivals in 2024, still 13% below 2019, with +8% growth in 2025 and 34.5% share of global aviation RPK.

The Middle East delivered solid full-year 2025 performance — total RPK growth of 6.8% and international RPK growth 
of 6.7%, with PLF improving 0.7 percentage points to 81.5% and 81.6% respectively — before experiencing an abrupt reversal in early 2026. In March 2026, traffic carried by Middle Eastern airlines contracted 58.6% year-on-year, with international RPK declining 60.8% and capacity falling 54.7%, following widespread airspace closures linked to heightened regional geopolitical tensions. PLF fell to 68.3% — the only region globally to record a load factor decline. Global capacity is expected to partially recover from May 2026, though Middle East-serving seats are projected to remain 18.3% below prior year levels. For BLS, this disruption has compressed near-term demand from applicants transiting Gulf hubs — particularly from the Indian subcontinent — and remains a key variable for the Company's revenue outlook in the current financial year.

Boeing's Commercial Market Outlook projects airlines will need over 44,000 new aircraft over the next 20 years, valued at USD 8.5 trillion.

to recover — with several key sub-markets still approximately 10% below 2019 levels, indicating substantial structural headroom. Visa and Consular 
Services IndustryThe visa and consular outsourcing industry has entered a phase of structural acceleration — governments worldwide are 
increasingly mandating specialist third-party providers to manage consular operations, reduce operational overhead, and deliver a superior applicant experience. What was once a niche administrative function has evolved into a multi-billion dollar global industry, underpinned by rising cross-border mobility, the digitalisation of government services, and the growing complexity of immigration regimes.
The total global visa services market — encompassing outsourced application processing, biometric services, document 
verification, courier, and value-added services — is currently valued at approximately USD 3.66 billion in CY2025, growing at a CAGR of 14.3% through 2033. The outsourced segment is growing faster, valued at approximately USD 3.2 billion in CY2025 and projected to reach USD 5.1 billion by 2033. The outsourced share of total applications has risen steadily from 22% in 2010 to 35% in 2021 to 38% in CY2024, and is projected at 50% by CY2029 — reflecting an accelerating structural shift towards outsourcing adoption globally. BLS International holds a 17% share by value and over 10% by volume in the global visa outsourcing market, excluding the United States.OVERVIEW

GLOBAL CONSULAR SERVICES MARKET GLOBAL VISA OUTSOURCING SERVICES MARKET — BY TYPE OF VISA
MARKET EVOLUTION — HISTORICAL AND PROJECTEDConsular outsourcing represents the highest-growth adjacent market within BLS's core service domain. The total global 
consular services market — encompassing passport, notarisation, attestation, legalisation, and related citizen services — was valued at USD 8.7 billion in 2024 and is forecast to reach USD 16.5 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 7.2%. Asia-Pacific is projected to register the highest regional CAGR of 9.1% between 2025 and 2033.
Tourist visas accounted for the largest share of the global outsourced visa market at 65% in CY2024, supported by the sustained recovery in international leisure travel and increasing adoption of e-visa services. Study visas represented 15% of the market, reflecting continued demand for overseas education, while business visas accounted for 10%, driven by the revival in corporate travel and expanding cross-border trade. Work visas contributed 9%, supported by rising skill-based migration, while the remaining 1% comprised diplomatic, transit and other specialised visa categories.
The structural shift is reflected clearly in historical data. Despite total visa applications contracting from 133 million 
in CY2019 to 121 million in CY2024 due to pandemic disruption and the residual contraction in some corridors, the outsourced share grew from approximately 27% to 38% over the same period — confirming that outsourcing adoption is a structural secular trend, not volume-dependent. The market is projected to return to 140 million total applications by CY2029 while the outsourced share reaches 50%, effectively doubling the absolute outsourced volume from ~35 million to ~70 million applications.Consular outsourcing is compounding at 32% annually from USD 156 million in CY2024 to a projected USD 634 million by CY2029 — the fastest-growing sub-segment within the visa and consular services value chain. This growth is driven by technological advancements in biometric authentication, personalised premium service offerings, the rise of subscription-based travel services, and a growing reliance on specialist providers for services that governments previously handled in-house. Asia-Pacific and the Middle East account for the largest share of incremental consular outsourcing demand, driven by rising outbound mobility and deepening bilateral diplomatic relationships.https:/ /marketintelo.com/report/consular-services-market

RESIDENCY AND INVESTMENT MIGRATION
OUTLOOKBLS International participates in the structurally growing investment migration segment through its wholly owned 
subsidiary, Citizenship Invest, acquired in October 2024 for Rs. 260 Crores (approximately USD 31 million). Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Dubai, Citizenship Invest has served more than 1,800 clients across 85 nationalities, maintaining a 99% application success rate against an industry average of approximately 80%.
The total global visa market is projected to reach USD 7.7 billion by CY2029. The outsourced segment is forecast to 
grow at a 14% CAGR, with outsourced visa applications reaching 70 million at an 8% CAGR by CY2029. The outlook is further shaped by the adoption of AI and automation for processing efficiency, biometric integration across application centres, the expansion of e-visa systems, and premium service differentiation as a growth driver. Outsourcing players that deliver efficiency, reduce government costs, and elevate the applicant experience are structurally well-positioned in this expanding market.
BLS International's strategic position: With a 17% market share by value (ex-USA), 10%+ by volume, operations across 
66 countries, and the addition of Citizenship Invest in the investment migration segment, BLS is positioned to benefit from each of these structural drivers — rising visa volumes, accelerating outsourcing adoption, premium service demand, and the globalisation of high-net-worth mobility.The investment migration market enters 2026 facing a more uncertain regulatory environment, with the European Union hardening its stance on citizenship-by-investment programmes and the United States imposing travel restrictions on citizens of select nations operating such schemes. These developments reinforce the importance of jurisdictional diversification and the sustained demand for specialised advisory and processing expertise — precisely the capabilities that Citizenship Invest delivers.INVESTMENT MIGRATION — STRUCTURAL TAILWINDS
The global investment migration industry surpassed USD 30 billion in annual market value during 2024, maintaining a steady 12% growth rate year over year, with over 80 countries now offering some form of investment migration programme. Henley & Partners' Private Wealth Migration Report 2025 recorded 142,000 millionaire relocations in 2025 — a new high — with forecasts pointing to 165,000 in 2026, the largest migration of wealth on record.

For two decades, BLS International Services Ltd. has built its reputation on a singular mandate — making governments 
more accessible to their citizens. Operational since 2005, the Company today stands as the world’s second-largest outsourced visa and consular services provider, operating across 80+ countries and serving 46+ client governments across Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, and the Middle East. Since inception, BLS has processed over 490 million applications globally, reflecting the scale, operational depth, and long-standing trust the Company has established with governments and applicants worldwide.
Beyond the breadth of its global footprint, BLS is distinguished by the trust and responsibility embedded in its mandate. 
The Company operates at the sovereign interface — where a government’s obligations to its citizens and the global community are translated into a seamless service experience. From visa processing and biometric enrolment to passport renewals, document attestation, and citizenship and residency-by-investment facilitation, BLS manages processes that are administratively complex, security-sensitive, and profoundly personal to the individuals it serves.
Domestically, BLS E-Services extends this philosophy into India’s grassroots, delivering Business Correspondent, 
E-Governance, Assisted Digital Services and Loan Distribution to citizens in urban and rural communities alike- turning last mile access into a scalable, technology driven business ecosystem.COMPANY OVERVIEW

KEY BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS
The Visa & Consular Services segment offers comprehensive outsourced visa processing, document verification and 
attestation, biometric enrolment, passport renewals, e-Visa solutions, and related value-added services (VAS). The segment serves 46 client governments including Spain, India, Italy, Germany, the United States, UAE, Slovakia, Cyprus, and the Czech Republic, among others.  Key contracts include the global visa outsourcing contracts for Spain and Slovakia, the Ministry of External Affairs (India) contract for Indian Visa Application Centres in China, and key visa service mandates for Italy and Cyprus.

application growing 13.7% to Rs. 3,302. EBITDA margins expanded substantially from 14.6% in FY22 to 40.1% in FY26, reflecting the Company's successful transition from a partner-run model to a self-managed model, investments in technology, and increasing operational leverage.BLS E-Services Limited is a fast-growing subsidiary that extends BLS International's government-to-citizen (G2C) proposition into India's digital landscape. The segment provides essential banking products and financial services to rural and remote communities under the Government of India's Financial Inclusion Program (Business Correspondent), e-Governance services (Aadhaar enrolment, PAN, birth and death certificates, property registrations), Assisted E-Services (PoS solutions, ticketing, assisted e-commerce), and loan distribution (personal, business, and other credit products through Aadifidelis Solutions). As of FY26, the Digital Services segment generated revenues of Rs. 1,158 Crores, reflecting a 114.4% YoY growth, significantly accelerated by the consolidation of Aadifidelis Solutions.   Given that BLS E-Services Limited is a separately listed entity, further details of the business and industry can be assessed in its annual report available on its website as well as stock exchanges.

STRENGTHS
OPPORTUNITIESWith a presence across 80+ countries and partnerships with 46 client governments, BLS has reinforced 
its standing as a dependable outsourcing partner for sensitive, citizen-facing government work. The successful renewal of the Attestation & Apostille Services contract with India’s Ministry of External Affairs, alongside new wins such as the Indian Visa Application Centres across China, underscores the Company’s established credibility and the trust it commands among sovereign clients.A cluster of the Company’s major visa-outsourcing contracts come up for renewal over the next two years, representing an estimated USD 1-2 Billion opportunity. Because BLS already holds operational incumbency, data history, and embassy relationships on most of these mandates, it starts the renewal cycle from a position of strength rather than having to win cold.
All of the Company’s visa application centres operate on leased premises, keeping the business capital-light and allowing new centres to be deployed quickly in response to contract wins. This operational agility, demonstrated through the rapid rollout of new centres in FY26, continues to be a meaningful advantage when bidding for time-sensitive government tenders.Beyond visas, services such as passport renewal, document attestation, apostille, and notarial work are structurally less cyclical than tourist-visa volumes and carry their own renewal economics, as evidenced by the MEA Attestation & Apostille contract renewal. Expanding this category across more client governments diversifies BLS’s revenue away from pure travel-cycle sensitivity.Most of the Company’s government contracts run for five to ten years on an exclusive basis, ensuring no overlap with competing vendors within a given region and providing strong visibility into future revenue and profitability. New long-term mandates secured in FY26, including the five-year global contract from the Slovak Republic and the expanded Cyprus mandate across multiple geographies, extend this visibility further into the coming years.Digital Services revenue grew 114.4% in FY26, but EBITDA margin in the segment compressed to 7.0% from 11.1%, reflecting the cost of rapidly scaling touchpoints and integrating new businesses. The opportunity in FY27 and beyond is to convert that scale into margin — cross-selling loan distribution, e-governance, and assisted e-commerce services through the same 1,55,000+ touchpoint network rather than running each as a separate cost line.
Having proven execution on the UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra order, BLS is positioned to bid for similar state-level and national identity-infrastructure mandates beyond Bihar’s Permanent Enrolment Centres, as more Indian states and potentially other countries digitise citizen-identity programmesAs more tenders explicitly weight technical and security capability, BLS’s continued investment in AI-driven document verification, fraud-resistant waitlisting, and automated workflow management can be used as a differentiator in financial bidding processes — turning a cost centre into a basis for winning higher-value mandates rather than competing purely on price.BLS’s competitive strength is increasingly underpinned by its technology stack — spanning AI-led identity verification, liveness and anti-spoofing checks aligned with ISO/IEC 30107, and GDPR-aligned data handling — which strengthens both processing accuracy and government confidence in the Company’s ability to safeguard sensitive citizen data. These capabilities are increasingly cited as a differentiator in financial bidding processes, reinforcing the Company’s eligibility for technically demanding sovereign mandates.The award of Indian Visa Application Centres across China for the Ministry of External Affairs, the five-year Slovak Republic global contract, and the Cyprus mandate spanning Russia, China, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Southeast Asia together open multiple new country corridors. Each new corridor is also a foothold from which BLS can pitch adjacent consular and digital services to the same client government.Global Reach and Sovereign Trust Re-tender Wave Worth USD 1-2 Billion

THREATS
Risk: Digital Services EBITDA margin fell to 7.0% 
in FY26 from 11.1% in FY25 even as revenue more than doubled. If newly acquired and rapidly scaled businesses such as Aadifidelis and the BC network continue to be integrated at lower near-term profitability, blended consolidated margins could come under continued pressure before synergies are realised.Risk: New operations such as the Indian VACs in China and the Cyprus contract spanning Russia, South Africa, Kazakhstan and several Southeast Asian markets extend BLS’s exposure to jurisdictions with relatively higher geopolitical and currency volatility than its more established Western European and North American operations.
Risk: A meaningful share of incremental FY26 growth is linked to a small number of large mandates — notably the UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra order and the consolidation of Aadifidelis. Any delay, scope reduction, or non-renewal of a single large government contract could have an outsized effect on growth and margin trajectories relative to a more granular, broadly distributed contract book.
Risk: The Company’s strategy of continued M&A — 
exemplified by the Aadifidelis consolidation in FY26 — introduces integration risk: differing data systems, compliance regimes, and working-capital cycles across acquired entities (particularly in lending and BC operations, which do not enjoy the same upfront-fee, negative-working-capital characteristics as the core visa business) could dilute the Group’s historically strong cash conversion.
Risk: As BLS’s digital footprint widens — spanning 
biometric data, Aadhaar enrolment records, loan applicant data, and embassy visa data across more countries and more subsidiaries simultaneously — the attack surface for data breaches and the regulatory exposure under frameworks such as GDPR and India’s data protection regime both increase.Mitigation: Management is targeting cross-sell across the combined touchpoint network and centralisation of back-office and technology costs across the Digital Services businesses, aiming to lift segment margins as integration matures rather than treating each acquisition as a standalone cost centre.Mitigation: The Company’s asset-light, leased-premises model limits capital at risk in any single country, while a deliberately diversified portfolio means that disruption in any one corridor is designed to have a contained rather than Group-wide impact.
Mitigation: BLS continues to diversify its government-client base across geographies and service lines — visa, consular, identity infrastructure, and digital/BC services — so that no single sovereign mandate determines overall Company performance, while also bidding aggressively for the next wave of contract renewals to keep the pipeline broad.
Mitigation: BLS evaluates targets for strategic 
fit with its core G2C and citizen-services thesis before acquisition, integrates finance and technology functions centrally post-acquisition, and continues to report segment-level financials to allow early identification of any subsidiary under cash or compliance strain.
Mitigation: Continued investment in ISO 
27001-aligned information security, GDPR-aligned data handling, and AI-led fraud and identity-verification controls is intended to keep pace with the expanding scope of sensitive data the Company now manages across its visa, consular, and digital businesses.
Margin Pressure in the Scaling Digital Segment Currency and Geopolitical Exposure from Expanded Footprint
Concentration Risk from Large Single Contracts

Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 36.7% year-on-year to ₹2,998 crore, driven by higher visa application volumes, contribution from recently acquired businesses, and continued expansion in digital-led services. FINANCIAL RATIOS – CONSOLIDATED Human Resource 
Corporate Social Responsibility
Risk ManagementBLS International’s people strategy in FY 2025-26 centred on building a diverse, capable, and engaged global workforce 
in step with the Company’s expanding international footprint. Diversity and inclusion remained embedded in hiring, career development, and performance management, with continued emphasis on local talent acquisition across operating geographies alongside structured leadership development through LEAP for first-time managers and LEAD for experienced leaders. The Company strengthened its learning ecosystem through wider access to LinkedIn Learning and the iCOACH internal trainer programme, while competency-based talent reviews, critical role identification, and Individual Development Plans reinforced succession planning and leadership readiness. Employee engagement and recognition were advanced through the “Path Finders” programme and Value Cards, global collaboration forums such as the Gurugram Global Operations Offsite, and continued investment in physical, mental, and financial wellbeing through country-specific medical cover, flexible work practices, and performance-linked rewards. Together, these initiatives strengthened frontline readiness, leadership depth, and employee retention, supporting the Company’s service quality and long-term growth agenda.
During FY 2025-26, BLS International deployed Rs. 69 Lakhs towards its Women Empowerment Programme, 
implemented through Sansthanam Abhay Daanam across centres in Noida and Maharashtra, reaching 720 beneficiaries, of whom 85% belonged to vulnerable and marginalised groups. The programme combined livelihood-focused skill training — spanning handloom and weaving, tailoring and knitting, pottery, and digital literacy — with the Gurukul Education Centres, which provided free education and extra-curricular development to women and underprivileged children. These initiatives translated into tangible outcomes, including documented cases of beneficiaries securing stable income through trades such as handloom work and stitching, while the full CSR allocation for the year was utilised with no unspent balance, reflecting disciplined programme execution and full compliance with the Company’s CSR commitments.
Risk management is embedded within BLS International’s strategic framework and supports the Company’s long-term 
growth objectives. The Company follows an integrated approach to identifying, assessing, and managing risks and opportunities across its operations. Strategic decisions are guided by principles of sustainable growth, operational agility, and responsible business practices. Across all business segments, BLS International remains committed to maintaining high standards of ethics, transparency, and governance in line with its Code of Conduct.

Internal Controls and Quality Governance
Cautionary StatementBLS International has implemented a comprehensive governance and control environment designed to protect 
organisational assets, strengthen operational effectiveness, and support adherence to applicable regulatory standards. Oversight of these mechanisms is led by the Company’s quality and compliance function, which supervises implementation across both visa application centres and corporate operations.
The framework encompasses structured risk evaluation procedures, defined control protocols, transparent reporting 
and communication channels, periodic independent reviews, and continuous performance monitoring. Regular internal assessments are undertaken to measure the efficiency of business operations, information security practices, and compliance with globally recognised standards, including ISO 9001:2015, ISO 27001:2013, ISO 14001:2015, and CMMI certifications.
Review processes extend across essential operational areas such as applicant servicing, document handling, 
cybersecurity safeguards, workplace safety protocols, and technology systems management. In addition, BLS International conducts detailed service quality assessments, customer experience reviews, and focused capability-building programmes to identify gaps, strengthen service standards, and ensure timely remedial action wherever required.
Through this integrated approach, the Company reinforces operational transparency, mitigates compliance risks, and 
maintains high standards of service reliability and corporate governance.

3. S TATE OF THE COMPANY’S AFFAIRS
 BLS International Services Ltd. is a globally trusted 
service partner for governments and citizens, with a legacy spanning two decades since its inception in 2005. The company partners with more than 46 governments client, including Diplomatic Missions, Embassies and Consulates, and operates across more than 100 countries. It is the largest publicly listed player in Visa and Consular Services. BLS International leverages AI, biometrics, intelligent document processing and digital platforms to enhance service delivery, security and operational efficiency.
 BLS International holds global certifications including 
CMMI DEV ML5 V3.0, SVC ML5 V3.0, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 14001:2015. It has been recognised among India’s Most Valuable Companies by Business Today, Forbes Asia’s Best Under a Billion, Fortune India’s Next 500, and Fortune India’s Emerging

c. A brief on types of customers
 BLS Int ernational serves a diverse customer base comprising individual applicants, citizens, government 
authorities, embassies, consulates, diplomatic missions, and other institutional clients. The company’s 
customers mainly include individuals seeking visa, passport, consular, attestation, biometric, e-visa, citizen services, banking correspondence and aadhaar enrolment, update and other miscellaneous aadhaar services at ASK. It also serves government and diplomatic clients by providing outsourced, technology-enabled service delivery support through application centres and digital platforms.
 In addition, BLS Int ernational caters to customers using digital, e-governance, and value-added services, such 
as form filling assistance, courier support, SMS updates, photocopying, premium services, and other applicant convenience services, wherever applicable.
 Ov erall, the company’s customer profile includes both B2G customers, such as governments and diplomatic 
missions, and B2C customers, such as citizens and individual service applicants.

Operational Execution RiskRisk: Failure to execute leads to inefficiencies, cost overruns, stakeholder dissatisfaction. 6 Currency Fluctuation RiskRisk: Revenue/profit volatility, cost unpredictability.
Opportunity: 
Natural hedging benefits, pricing optimization, geographic arbitrage.With operations spanning multiple geographies, BLS International is exposed to foreign exchange fluctuations that may impact revenues, costs and reported financial performance. Variations in currency exchange rates could affect earnings 
from international operations and cross-border transactions.BLS International employs a currency hedging policy aligned with industry best practices to mitigate the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on receivables, projected revenue, and other current assets and liabilities. The hedging strategy is periodically reviewed and adjusted to align with prevailing market conditions. The Company’s negative working capital model — where processing fees are collected upfront before services are rendered — significantly reduces receivables exposure and limits the duration of currency risk on revenue streams.Negative: Multi-year contract devaluation, Government fee denomination mismatch, Revenue-cost timing mismatch, Foreign subsidiary translation losses. 
Positive: Contract 
appreciation in strong currencies, Multi-currency portfolio benefits, Multi-currency account structures

This framework provides a systematic approach to identifying, assessing, and mitigating workplace hazards, ultimately fostering a culture of safety and well-being among all employees.

 BLS ’s Occupational Health and Safety Management System is designed in accordance with the ISO 45001:2018 
standards. It adopts a comprehensive and structured methodology for assessing risks associated with both routine and non-routine tasks. This system empowers process owners, who work closely with safety specialists, to actively identify potential hazards and risks that may arise during operations. With a focus on fostering a safe working environment, these stakeholders are tasked with ensuring that adequate control measures are
